passage:
The power had gone out in the last period, and the classroom was hot and dim. Hansa noticed Aadhya staring at her art sheet, lips pressed together. It was a lovely peacock, with 'Good, but colour outside lines' written in red.
Hansa almost said, 'That's nothing!' She wouldn't have minded one bit. Then she remembered how Mummy had asked her yesterday, 'What happened?' before saying anything else.
'What happened?' Hansa whispered.
'I worked on it all Sunday,' Aadhya said. 'Art is my one good thing.'
Hansa thought about that. Art wasn't her thing, but maths was. She'd feel awful if Sir wrote red lines on her maths.
'It's still the best peacock in class,' she said. 'Want help with the edges next time?'

qa.q: What was written in red on Aadhya's art sheet?
Why did Hansa almost say 'That's nothing!'?
qa.a: Hansa wouldn't have minded such a comment herself, so at first she didn't see why Aadhya was upset.

qa.q: What turning point helped Hansa understand Aadhya?
qa.a: Remembering Mummy asking 'What happened?' made Hansa ask first, and hearing that art is Aadhya's one good thing let her compare it to her own maths.

qa.q: How might Aadhya feel when Hansa offers help with the edges?
qa.a: Aadhya may feel understood and supported rather than brushed off, since Hansa took the hurt seriously.

grounding: Shows a child starting to understand why a classmate is upset when she herself would not be, asking what happened and offering help, as an adult had modelled.

passage:
In the colony park after school, Lalremsiami sat on the swing but didn't swing. Urmila, nine, wanted to play catch. 'Come on!'
'I'm not in the mood.'
Urmila was puzzled. Ma'am had only changed the seating. Urmila didn't care where she sat. But her Papa, walking by with the vegetable bag, stopped. 'Siami, what happened, beta?'
'They moved me away from Grace. She's the only one I talk to in class.'
Urmila watched Papa ask and listen, and it clicked. For Siami, a seat wasn't just a seat.
'Tomorrow at lunch you can sit with me and Grace,' Urmila said. 'Every day, if you want.'
Siami pushed off with her feet, just a little.

qa.q: Who did Lalremsiami get moved away from?
qa.a: Grace, the only one Siami talks to in class.

qa.q: Why was Urmila puzzled at first?
qa.a: Urmila didn't care where she sat, so she couldn't see why a seating change would upset Lalremsiami.

qa.q: What turning point helped Urmila see things through Lalremsiami's eyes?
qa.a: Watching Papa ask what happened and listen made it click that a seat wasn't just a seat, so Urmila offered to sit together at lunch.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami feel when pushing off on the swing a little?
qa.a: Siami may feel a bit lighter and less alone, knowing Urmila understood.

grounding: Shows a child learning to see why another child is upset about something she would not mind, after an adult models asking and listening.
